free_tier.stated: subdomains under duckdns.org with a token API, IPv4, IPv6 and TXT support

per_object_cap.stated: the number of subdomains per account is about 5, a third-party figure; DuckDNS publishes no number

retention.stated: a record persists until updated or cleared with clear=true, provided the account is used

interface_detail: a single HTTPS GET per update; the token is a query parameter
tooling: curl, any DDNS client, a router's built-in DuckDNS provider
chaining: a name for a home IP or a tunnel endpoint, and nothing else: no certificate automation and no proxying

limits.value: about 5 subdomains, a third-party figure; DuckDNS publishes no number

reliability_note: a bad token returns HTTP 200 with the body KO, so a status-only check reports success on a failed update
confidence_note: the update endpoint was called today with an empty token and answered 200 KO, which proves both the endpoint and the failure shape. The subdomain cap is third-party.

evidence.proved: 200 with a two-byte body 'KO'. A 200 is not success; the rejection is in the body
the update URL, IPv4 and IPv6 parameters, the TXT form, and clear=true to delete records; a TXT record applies to all sub-subdomains under the name

notes: A DuckDNS name cannot be a Cloudflare zone, so it cannot carry a Tunnel, Email Routing or Universal SSL. It is a dynamic-DNS tool, not a name a service can live on.
